title: client-probe-chunk-timing-repro
content:
Goal: quick personal playbook to reproduce a client-observed streaming hiccup where SSE chunks stall for ~5-15s intermittently. Keep this as a lightweight repro and list of probes I tried so others can pick up.

Symptoms observed (from customer logs and local repro):
- Client sees a few initial SSE events quickly, then a pause of ~5-15s, then a burst of many events at once.
- curl --no-buffer shows the same pattern when attached to the same proxy path.
- No obvious 500 or error status; connection remains open and then resumes.
- More common when payloads are small (50-800 bytes) and high concurrency (20+ streams).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Proxy/nginx/ingress buffering or buffering heuristics (proxy_buffering, chunk sizes, flush intervals) causing delay until buffer full or timer fires.
2) TCP-level delayed ACK/Nagle interaction when small writes are issued from the runtime (coalescing at sender or delayed ack at receiver) causing bursts.
3) Runtime batching combined with continuous batching heuristics — runtime holds tokens to amortize kernel overhead then flushes.
4) Envoy upstream flow-control/backpressure windowing interaction with HTTP/1 chunked encoding vs HTTP/2 DATA frames.
5) Client-side EventSource polyfill or browser socket scheduling (less likely for curl repro).

Environment/paths to repro:
- Local dev runtime: http://localhost:8080/v1/stream (direct runtime)
- With nginx reverse-proxy in front: http://localhost:9080/stream-proxy -> proxy_pass http://localhost:8080/v1/stream
- With Envoy (k8s): route to cluster runtime-service port 8080, HTTP/1.1 passthrough
- Test clients: curl (mac/linux), nodejs EventSource (eventsource polyfill v1.1.1), Python requests + iter_lines

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Start runtime locally with a small model mock that emits SSE for each token using chunked encoding. Use the test harness flag --stream-debug to force small writes.
2) Run direct curl test:
   curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --no-buffer "http://localhost:8080/v1/stream?prompt=test&simulate=small-chunks"
   Observed: initial event within 100ms, then 8s silence, then many lines.

3) Run via nginx proxy (default config):
   - Basic nginx conf snippet used in test:
     proxy_buffering on;
     proxy_buffers 8 4k;
     proxy_busy_buffers_size 8k;
     proxy_request_buffering off;
   curl -v --no-buffer "http://localhost:9080/stream-proxy?prompt=test"
   Observed: same pause but slightly longer.

4) Variant: nginx with proxy_buffering off:
   proxy_buffering off;
   curl -v --no-buffer "http://localhost:9080/stream-proxy?prompt=test"
   Observed: much smoother stream, smaller pauses. Strong signal that proxy buffering contributes.

Commands I used to probe TCP behavior:
- TCP dump around connection to see packetization:
  sudo tcpdump -i lo0 -w /tmp/sse-repro.pcap tcp port 8080
- Inspect pcap in Wireshark: saw small TCP segments from server followed by delayed ACKs from client (often ~40ms) and occasional coalesced payloads.

Commands and quick client tests (copy/paste):
- curl raw:
  curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --no-buffer "http://localhost:8080/v1/stream?simulate=small-chunks" 2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'

- curl via nginx -> show timing between Received bytes:
  (python one-liner to print timestamps per line):
  curl -s -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --no-buffer "http://localhost:9080/stream-proxy?simulate=small-chunks" | python -u -c "import sys, time\nfor l in sys.stdin:\n    print(time.time(), l.rstrip())"

- node EventSource probe (node 18):
  cat <<'NODE' > es-probe.js
  const EventSource = require('eventsource');
  const es = new EventSource('http://localhost:9080/stream-proxy?simulate=small-chunks');
  let t0 = Date.now();
  es.onmessage = (e) => {
    console.log(Date.now()-t0, 'ms', e.data.slice(0,80));
  };
  es.onerror = (err) => console.error('ERR', err);
NODE
  node es-probe.js

Runtime logging snippets (from local runtime with --stream-debug):
[2026-02-18T14:02:33.421Z] stream: write_chunk 128 bytes -> client_socket=127.0.0.1:53622 inflight_writes=2
[2026-02-18T14:02:33.425Z] stream: write returned 128 (EAGAIN=false)
[2026-02-18T14:02:33.467Z] stream: write_chunk 64 bytes -> client_socket=127.0.0.1:53622 inflight_writes=3
[2026-02-18T14:02:38.512Z] stream: resumed after 1 chunk flush (timer expired), wrote 1024 bytes
(note the ~5s gap between the 2 small writes and the flush)

Nginx access logs during repro (truncated):
127.0.0.1 - - [18/Feb/2026:14:02:33 +0000] "GET /stream-proxy?simulate=small-chunks HTTP/1.1" 200 0 "-" "curl/7.86"
(nginx does not show chunk timings but proxy logs show periods of inactivity)

What changed that improved behavior in quick experiments:
- Turning proxy_buffering off in nginx removed large pauses in most cases.
- Forcing the runtime to set TCP_CORK off / toggling socket write coalescing reduced bursts (dev hacky flag).
- Increasing chunk sizes from 128->1024 bytes made pauses less frequent (less Nagle/delayed ACK interaction).

Other probes tried (and results):
- HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1: with Envoy doing HTTP/2 to upstream, saw similar pauses but framing differences made analysis harder. When we forced HTTP/1.1 end-to-end, behavior was clearer that chunking+proxy buffering mattered.
- Keepalive and SO_LINGER tweaks: no impact on pattern.
- Using `stdbuf -oL` on a simple server to flush writes: proved that explicit flush on server avoided pause.
- Browser reproduction: harder because browser schedules rendering; but node/curl repro is reliable and reproducible.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does default nginx proxy_buffering on cause longer holds for small chunks? (suspect buffer policy + timer; need to confirm proxy_buffer_size thresholds and buffer fill timers)
- Are there Envoy settings equivalent to proxy_buffering (brotli/HTTP filters) that could add similar delay? We saw hints in envoy buffer stats but not deterministic.
- Is our runtime's continuous batching heuristic too aggressive when response size is small and latencies are otherwise low? Might need threshold by elapsed time instead of by token count.

Immediate next steps for me (hands-on):
- Re-run pcap with nginx proxy_buffering off/on and compare tcpdump timings; annotate pcap with write syscalls from runtime.
- Create small Go server that emits SSE in tight loops to isolate runtime vs proxy behavior.
- Test Envoy with http_connection_manager settings: stream_idle_timeout / max_response_headers_count / upstream_flush_on_body_chunk.
- Add a temporary runtime flag to always set TCP_NODELAY and expose it as TEST_ONLY to see impact across k8s.

Notes for handoff to infra team:
- If you see customer reports about "event stream stalls then floods" try to repro with curl --no-buffer and check proxy_buffering on the ingress. Turning it off often mitigates.
- Consider a short runbook: for streaming endpoints, set proxy_buffering off and proxy_request_buffering off; for Envoy add a config to flush on chunk.

Quick TL;DR for standups: short chunks + proxy buffering + TCP coalescing -> intermittent stall. Workaround: disable buffering or increase chunk size / force flush.

Timestamped experiments (quick log of runs):
- 2026-02-18 13:55 - Repro on local runtime (direct) confirmed
- 2026-02-18 14:05 - Repro via nginx (buffering on) reproduced pause
- 2026-02-18 14:18 - nginx proxy_buffering off removed most pauses
- 2026-02-20 09:12 - Verified Envoy shows similar effect; need deeper config checks

If anyone picks this up: I left pcap + runtime logs at /tmp/sse_repro_logs_{date} on my VM and a small go prototype under runtime/experiments/sse-flush-probe (not yet pushed).
